content.markdown:
# Site-specific monitoring and leachate containment for Zelena Petlja

## Verified facts
- The company reports an inspectorate order requiring four groundwater monitoring wells within 120 days and a remediation proposal, with a stated deadline in late June 2024. This is the supplied historical timetable, not a confirmed current deadline. [F1]
- The company's latest hydrogeological sketch dates from 1993. It reports that contamination extent and seasonal groundwater-flow directions are unknown. [F2]
- The company reports a liner not designed for liquid retention and an in-house COD result of 3,400 mg/L. It seeks an inspectorate-acceptable containment and treatment proposal, not monitoring alone. [F3]
- The company states that it has two technicians with process-engineering backgrounds, no dedicated research budget, and no laboratory beyond its basic wet-chemistry bench for leachate monitoring. [F4]
- Zorić lists openness to joint company projects on groundwater remediation. Her availability-related note concerns reduced teaching in 2025/26; it does not establish capacity for the company's stated 2024 deadline. [F5]
- Zorić's research supports multi-indicator groundwater monitoring and moisture-calibrated infiltration modelling. Her transfer-station study warns that mean-annual containment designs may underestimate peak infiltration by up to 40% in that climatic setting. [F6]
- Her passive-drain research reports field capture efficiencies of 84–97% at three Vojvodina installations. Her zeolite research concerns ammonium removal in laboratory columns using leachate from two Vojvodina sites. [F7]

## Potential benefits
- For the company: The first experiment could establish whether available evidence supports defensible well placement and identify the investigation or treatment gaps preventing an acceptable remediation proposal.
- For the researcher: Subject to agreement and access, the project could provide site measurements, sediments and leachate for testing how transferable alluvial-aquifer monitoring and containment methods are to this storage yard.

## Our inference
- This suggests a useful joint project linking field investigation to regulatory design, conditional on confirming Zorić's availability for the actual delivery period.
- The site's sediments, aquifer geometry and seasonal gradients may differ from the research sites. Four wells may leave plume boundaries unresolved; one campaign cannot establish seasonal reversals. Transferring published parameters or drain charts without local checks would therefore be risky.
- Interception would not itself demonstrate treatment of the COD burden, and ammonium-column results do not establish COD removal or field performance here. A funded investigation and separate source-control and treatability work are likely necessary.

## Proposed next steps
- Propose an initial four-week field-to-model test, subject to the current legal timetable and procurement feasibility. The company would supply records and coordinate access; Zorić would propose survey, sampling and model protocols. Compare the 1993-sketch conceptual baseline with surveyed groundwater heads, borehole sediments and quality-assured leachate/groundwater COD, chloride, ammonium and conductivity. Use separate tuning and later evaluation rounds, checking their independence. Test local hydraulic properties rather than importing published values. A negotiable screening target is head error below 10% of surveyed head range on withheld observations, reporting measurement uncertainty and unresolved plume boundaries. Go/no-go would concern the best configuration tested, not a named model: proceed only if evidence supports defensible well placement, resources and authorised delivery are available, and four installed wells plus an inspectorate-accepted containment/treatment proposal remain achievable by the verified deadline. Otherwise escalate immediately for regulatory agreement and additional investigation rather than claim compliance.
- Propose source-leakage controls alongside investigation, with safety and regulatory review. Compare site-leachate treatment candidates against an untreated control using separate tuning and evaluation aliquots. If ammonium warrants zeolite testing, measure breakthrough, hydraulic performance, COD and residual-management needs; negotiate concentration and capacity targets from inspectorate requirements before testing. Do not select treatment on ammonium removal alone.
- Propose a funded scope covering drilling, surveys, external analyses, monitoring and documentation, with named authorised contractors and signatories. Agree seasonal follow-up and any additional investigation with the inspectorate. Assign operation, maintenance and collected-leachate responsibilities before recommending implementation.

## Open questions
- What is the current order and compliance status, including the four wells, submission, applicable deadline and inspectorate acceptance criteria?
- Can Zorić confirm availability for this joint project's actual delivery window?
- Can the company supply the order, sketch, site and utility plans, liner and waste records, original analytical quality-control records, and permissions for boundary-area investigation?
- What funding, procurement arrangements and authorised delivery team can cover investigation, immediate containment, treatment trials and continuing operation?
